persons.name: Sarah
persons.harm: Over a roughly eight-month relationship and engagement (Sept 2017 to May 2018) her fiance love-bombed, gaslit and isolated her, posed for months as a fake married couple ('Kimmy and Brian') to manipulate and body-shame her, used scripture to turn her against her family, kicked and injured her dog, and controlled shared money. After the breakup he stalled refunds from their joint wedding fund, tried to log into her accounts, and charged flights to her old credit card.
persons.outcome_quote: We're going to come in guns blazing and we're going to get you out of Sacramento and we're not going to treat this like a breakup. We're treating this like a rescue.
persons.notes: The abuse ended because Sarah, her family and roommates found the catfishing and she left (breakup Mother's Day weekend, May 2018). No institution brought it about, so the outcome is not_protected. Not coded as institutional contacts: (a) her cousin, a police officer, came with family and watched the perpetrator's house while they took her belongings out (s1-e8 @ 18:38). He acted as family, not as a police response, and the harm was not reported to police. (b) Her call to the bank about the joint newlywed-fund refunds he was stalling ('I contact the bank and within 24 hours, it's done', s1-e8 @ 24:45) was a routine account request, not a report of abuse. (c) Her texts to the perpetrator's brother, who replied 'through the lens' of his role as a church elder (s1-e9 @ 43:49), were to his family and not a complaint to a church body. She threatened several times to go to police or file for a restraining order or animal abuse report (s1-e9 @ 6:17, 26:13, 32:24; s1-e10 @ 65:37) but is never shown doing so. Evidence: texts, the confession text and the brother's texts are read on air. Family, roommates and the ex-fiancee are second witnesses. The host says everything was fact-checked, including vet visits (s1-e9 @ 51:55), and real Kimmy confirmed the robe order from her own records on air (s1-e10 @ 22:35).

coder_notes: Season 1 of Something Was Wrong: Sarah's engagement to a man the show calls by a pseudonym (a perpetrator name, written here as [perpetrator]), 14 numbered episodes plus a trailer, a therapist bonus episode and the SWW Live Sacramento recording. All 8 chunk files were read to their last line. Main finding: almost none of the harm in this season reached an institution with power over the perpetrator. No police report, court filing, restraining order or platform report was ever made about him. Sarah, the host and the host's friend each threatened to go to police or file for restraining orders, but none is shown doing so. Sarah's contacts are financial (bank, Southwest), therapeutic and a veterinarian. Her protection came from family, roommates and her own detective work. Other women harmed by the same man (first ex-fiancee, Lulu, Lindsay, the summer-2018 girlfriend, real Kimmy and Brian) all dealt with it privately: blocking, cutting contact, a private cease-and-desist letter. Animal abuse of Sarah's dog Maple and his dog Finn is part of Sarah's harm record (animals are not person records). Judgment calls: (1) the cousin who is a police officer and watched the house during the move-out is treated as family, not a police contact; (2) the private attorney letter from real Kimmy and Brian is not an institutional contact; (3) Lindsay's earlier abusive marriage, Tiffany's childhood abuse and the DV expert's story come from expert/live segments and are recorded as separate person records, at low or medium confidence; (4) very thin voicemails (Ray, Allison, the high-school caller) are recorded at low confidence. Season 2's 'T' appears at the live show but her story is withheld for spoilers, so she is not recorded. Unassigned folder: I read the index only; no episode appeared related. Several quotes run across a transcript line break, where a [mm:ss] timestamp marker sits in the text; the marker is left out of the quote, and nothing else is changed. A second usage-limit interruption came after all reading was done and the JSON was written; afterwards I re-verified all quotes.
